Read return alongside risk

The final balance does not describe every experience within the period. Closing-equity drawdown and the treatment of costs provide essential context.

A closing-equity measure

The supplied report measures maximum drawdown from a prior closing-equity peak to a subsequent trough. It records the deepest trough on March 13, 2026. Its method makes no allowance for intraday excursions, so this figure does not describe the largest possible intraday loss.

What the material establishes

This page presents the supplied report and its historical equity series. It does not establish an independently audited account, current live performance, or a link between this history and the separate trading demonstrations. The original PDF remains available for inspection.

Definitions, costs & sources

The capital base matters. The source report distinguishes deployed capital from account equity and includes a modelled slippage allowance in costs.

Return on opening equity
Trading profit for the period divided by opening account equity of NOK 250,000. The opening value, closing value and period profit reconcile in the canonical summary.
Session return on deployed capital
The source defines this as session net profit divided by the notional capital put to work during that session. It is not the return on the full account.
Session return on account equity
The source compounds session profit against the prior closing account equity. The reported average is shown separately from the deployed-capital average.
Costs deducted at source
The PDF states that trading costs include commission per side lot, exchange and clearing fees, and a modelled slippage allowance of 1.10 basis points of notional. Modelled slippage is an assumption, not an observed execution charge.
